title: Composite board replaced by the resume board
question: Does a six-dimension percentile composite (rating 45%, form 10%, entrenchment 20%, offense 10%, activity 5%, durability 10%) rank fighters better than a resume score (rating 70% + quality ledger 30% - form penalty)?

method.instrument: retrospective reconstruction and review of the published boards
method.metric: concordance with later results; review of which dimensions carried ranking signal

candidate: Resume board (Option B): REAL rating 70%, quality ledger 30%, last-five form penalty, head-to-head and title-cycle placement rules

results.finding: four of the six composite dimensions carried no ranking signal and losses were counted three times (rating, form, durability)
results.outcome: resume board adopted as v1.0 and frozen Oct 1, 2026 (CHANGELOG.md 0.x and 1.0)

reason: The composite's extra dimensions added noise, not information; the resume score is interpretable and no less accurate.

title: Predictive Elo grid search and significance (the SSAC abstract result)
question: Which Elo specification predicts UFC bouts best out of sample, and is the performance-adjusted model better than results-only Elo?

method.baseline: results-only Elo tuned the same way (classic_tuned_params)
method.interval: paired event-block bootstrap 5,000 draws; exact McNemar on discordant bouts

results.gain: 0.0109 log loss, CI 0.0057 to 0.0162; McNemar p = 0.0025 (429 vs 344 discordant bouts)
results.calibration in the large: mean predicted first-listed 0.535 vs observed 0.572 (no corner term in v1.0)

reason: The pre-registered headline for the SSAC27 abstract; the interpretable site specification (0.6621 / 61.2%) is reported as a second specification only.

title: Board score to probability: the frozen slope 1.36
question: What logistic slope maps a REAL score difference to a win probability, for the pre-registered forward test?
reason: Frozen in PREREGISTRATION.md section 5; scored prospectively from Oct 2, 2026.

title: Shadow prediction model v1.1 (walk-forward Elo re-tune plus logistic layer)
question: Does re-tuning the Elo parameters walk-forward over 2011 onward, with a red-corner term and a logistic layer (age, layoff, experience, height, five rounds), beat the frozen v1.0 predictive model?

method.window: 2016-2026 (5,308 bouts), out of sample for both models 2020-2026 (3,404 bouts, 288 events)
method.baseline: v1.0 frozen predictive model on the same bouts

reason: Published only as a shadow in the picks ledger; adopted under PREREGISTRATION.md appendix B after 300 graded paired picks with a log-loss gain whose interval excludes zero.

title: Loss-handling candidates on 43 full boards (finding 1)
question: Does softening and making opponent-aware the three channels that charge a loss (ledger cost, form penalty, rating protection) cost accuracy?

method.instrument: resume_board.build at every third event date, every placement rule applied (head-to-head, title cycle), published order
method.bouts: 947 decided bouts between two fighters on the same divisional board
method.metric: concordance of the published order with the winner; log loss with the frozen v1.0 slope 1.36
method.baseline: v1.0 rules on the same bouts
method.interval: paired event-block bootstrap (all candidates' intervals against v1.0 straddle zero)

candidate.B+ (Bplus): ledger loss tiers [[5,0.25],[10,0.5],[15,0.75],[999,1.0]], dominant_extra 0.25; form buckets 2-3 0.10 / 1-4 0.30 / 0-5 0.40; bad-loss add-on 0.10 per last-five loss outside the top 10, cap 0.30
candidate.R: rating only (no ledger, no form penalty)
candidate.B, C, F: intermediate rule sets whose exact definitions were lost with the session context on Oct 20; results kept for the record

results.paired intervals: every candidate's 95% interval against v1.0 straddles zero on 947 bouts; rating-only is about 2 points worse, so the ledger and form carry information

face_validity.largest unintended moves: Jim Miller 11 to 19, Jalin Turner 15 to 23, Neil Magny 15 to 22

reason: v1.1 = B+0 with protection 0.30 adopted as a shadow board on face validity at equal measured accuracy (CHANGELOG 1.1). The 43-board instrument cannot separate the candidates (audit V1), which is why the 2014-2026 panel was built next.

title: Protected-loss multiplier and Kamaru Usman
question: Does raising the rating engine's protected-loss multiplier (0.15 in v1.0) move a 1-4 former champion with a sticky rating?

method.instrument: resume_board.build for Oct 18, 2026 (today's board) under v1.1 rules with the multiplier at 0.15, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50

results.Usman position: 5 at every setting; 7 needs about 20 more points
results.why: only two of his four losses were protected non-dominant first losses (Edwards 1, Du Plessis); Edwards 2 was already charged at 60% as a second straight loss and the Chimaev loss was unprotected and short-notice

reason: The multiplier is not the lever for this case; the rating channel's stickiness for a long-reigning champion is. Logged so the lever is not retried for this purpose.

title: Panel comparison: v1.0 rules vs B+0 under two engines
question: On a far larger instrument than the 43 boards, do the B+0 ledger and form rules change accuracy, and does protection 0.30 in the engine matter?

method.instrument: board_tune panel (src/mmalab/board_tune.py): one rating pass, boards every 14 days, score order without placement rules
method.bouts: 3,656 decided bouts between two fighters on the same divisional board at the preceding date
method.metric: pairwise concordance (ties 0.5); log loss through a one-parameter logistic map fitted on the bouts being scored (in-sample) unless stated
method.baseline: v1.0 rules on the same bouts
method.engines: v1.0 engine; engine with protected_loss_mult 0.30 (separate panel each)

results.reading: B+0 helps the whole population a little and hurts the top 15 by about 1.5 points (inside noise on 960 bouts); the engine change is neutral

reason: Both effects are small; the panel is the instrument for the walk-forward that follows. Note: these panels used the code before the dated roster files and the official-rank aliases were merged; the rebuilt panels (EXP-2026-10-20-06) supersede the absolute numbers.

title: Walk-forward tuning of the board rules, first pass (search blind spot)
question: Tuning the ledger, horizon, form and split one coordinate at a time on every year before the test year, how much held-out accuracy is available beyond v1.0?

method.instrument: board_tune panel (src/mmalab/board_tune.py): one rating pass, boards every 14 days, score order without placement rules
method.bouts: 3,656 decided bouts between two fighters on the same divisional board at the preceding date
method.metric: pairwise concordance (ties 0.5); log loss through a one-parameter logistic map fitted on the bouts being scored (in-sample) unless stated
method.baseline: v1.0 rules on the same bouts
method.protocol: test years 2017 to 2026; coordinate descent on training years (3 sweeps); slope for the test year fitted on training years only; 2,824 held-out bouts

candidate.search space: w_rating, horizon (steps or exponential), proof value, loss mode/tiers/extra/window/decay, hindsight mode and blends, form mode/buckets/tiers/cap/bad-loss

results.what the data chose: rating weight 0.75; quality wins at full value for one year then exponential decay with a 1.5-year time constant; losses charged flat for 15 years; a small tiered last-five penalty (0.05 to 0.20 per loss, cap 0.30)

reason: Real held-out gain of about 2 points of concordance, but the search had a blind spot: the loss tiers were never tried while loss mode was v1.0, and the hindsight blends were never tried while the mode was none (a mode switch alone changes nothing, so it was never accepted). Fixed by coupling those coordinates (IMPLIES in board_tune.py); rerun as EXP-2026-10-20-06. The chosen horizon (fast decay) also conflicts with the resume principle that long resumes keep their value, which the rerun tests as a separate preset.

title: Hindsight re-grading of results (curator's idea)
question: If the value of a win or the cost of a loss is graded partly by where the opponent stands now (or two years on) instead of only on fight night, does accuracy improve, and what does it do to the board?

method.instrument: board_tune panel (src/mmalab/board_tune.py): one rating pass, boards every 14 days, score order without placement rules
method.bouts: 3,656 decided bouts between two fighters on the same divisional board at the preceding date
method.metric: pairwise concordance (ties 0.5); log loss through a one-parameter logistic map fitted on the bouts being scored (in-sample) unless stated
method.baseline: v1.0 rules on the same bouts
method.note: in-sample grid on top of B+0, v1.0 engine panel; then full builds of today's board for face validity

candidate.modes: now_official (opponent's current official rank), now_rating (opponent's current REAL rating position in the bout's division), post_rating (rating position two years after the bout)
candidate.blends: alpha_win and alpha_loss in {1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25, 0}: weight on the fight-night grade

results.pattern: every setting improves log loss; more hindsight is better; the win side carries most of it

face_validity.Usman (WW): 5 at half and full hindsight by rating; 2 at full hindsight by two-year standing

reason: Small real gain, but it does the one thing the curator ruled out: it pulls down long resumes whose opponents have since faded (Vera 14 to 29, Adesanya 14 to 20 at full hindsight by rating) and leaves Usman at 5. Kept as a measured option in the harness; it would need a form that protects aged resumes (for example hindsight for wins younger than three years only) before it could be proposed.

title: Walk-forward tuning, second pass: coupled coordinates, free and resume presets
question: With the search blind spot fixed, how much held-out accuracy is available (a) with every rule free and (b) holding the resume principles fixed (quality wins keep full value for three or more years; losses count for at most six years), under the v1.0 engine and the 0.30-protection engine?

method.instrument: board_tune panel (src/mmalab/board_tune.py): one rating pass, boards every 14 days, score order without placement rules
method.bouts: 3,656 decided bouts between two fighters on the same divisional board at the preceding date
method.metric: pairwise concordance (ties 0.5); log loss through a one-parameter logistic map fitted on the bouts being scored (in-sample) unless stated
method.baseline: v1.0 rules on the same bouts
method.protocol: as EXP-2026-10-20-04 on panels rebuilt after the dated roster files and official-rank aliases were merged; presets free and resume; engines v1.0 and protected_loss_mult 0.30

results.stability of choices (free): horizon fast decay in 9 of 10 folds; loss tiers [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75] in 9 of 10; loss window 10 to 15 years; hindsight now_official in all 10 folds; rating weight 0.60 to 0.65
results.price of the resume principles: about 1.4 points of concordance and 0.0045 log loss held out (free 0.6052 / 0.6668 vs resume 0.5911 / 0.6713)
results.note: the 0.30-protection engine runs were dropped after the engine sweep (EXP-2026-10-20-07) showed the engine levers accuracy-neutral

reason: Both presets beat v1.0 out of sample (free +3.0 points, resume +1.6 points of concordance). The free rules are recency plus hindsight plus a long memory of losses, which the curator rejects for a resume board; the resume preset keeps three-year full credit and a six-year loss memory and still gains 1.6 points, but it chose hindsight (alpha 0.25) and a 1.0 blowout surcharge, so its face validity must be checked before it becomes a v1.2 proposal. No change to v1.1.

title: Rating-engine sweep (K, protection, consecutive-loss rule, protection ladder, no official ranks)
question: Which rating-engine settings predict better on the 2014-2026 panel with the v1.1 board rules fixed, and which of them move the anchors (Usman, Buckley, Adesanya, Vera)?

method.instrument: board_tune panel (src/mmalab/board_tune.py): one rating pass, boards every 14 days, score order without placement rules
method.bouts: 3,656 decided bouts between two fighters on the same divisional board at the preceding date
method.metric: pairwise concordance (ties 0.5); log loss through a one-parameter logistic map fitted on the bouts being scored (in-sample) unless stated
method.baseline: v1.0 rules on the same bouts
method.protocol: one panel per engine variant (13), v1.0 and v1.1 rules scored on the identical bouts, paired bootstrap of the v1.1-rule log loss against the base engine; anchors read from the last panel date in score order

results.reading: every engine lever is accuracy-neutral (largest log-loss change 0.0008); the protection multipliers, the ladder, K and the dominant-loss multiplier do not move the anchors except that removing official ranks (M4) puts Usman first in score order; the last six variants ran on data with five more bouts (same-name split merged mid-sweep), so their paired intervals are omitted

reason: The rating engine's protections are a cheap resume principle in predictive terms, as section 11 of the methodology already said; nothing here changes v1.1. M4 (model positions instead of official ranks) is neutral on accuracy and remains a philosophical option for a later version.

title: v1.1 retrospective reconstruction (its own snapshot directory)
question: Rebuilt as event-eve boards with every placement rule, what is v1.1's retrospective record on the same window as v1.0's reconstruction?

method.window: 127 event-eve snapshots Oct 2023 to Oct 16, 2026, plus today's
method.metric: concordance of the published order; log loss with the slope fitted on these snapshots (1.36 recorded in config/board_v1_1.yaml)
method.baseline: v1.0's own reconstruction (942 bouts, a different snapshot set, so not paired)

reason: In-sample for both versions; the prospective record from Oct 20, 2026 is the test (PREREGISTRATION.md appendix C).

title: Age and the rating channel: older favourites lose more often than they win
question: Does the board over-rank older fighters? Split the bouts by the higher-scored fighter's age and last-five losses and see how often he wins; then test a rating discount by age.

method.instrument: board_tune panel rebuilt Oct 20 (as-of roster files, official-rank aliases): one rating pass, boards every 14 days, score order without placement rules
method.bouts: 3,748 decided bouts between two fighters on the same divisional board; favourite = the higher v1.1 score
method.ages: date of birth from UFCStats (99.8% of fighter-dates)
method.metric: share of bouts won by the favourite (Wilson 95%); then concordance and log loss with the discount applied before interdecile scaling, in-sample
method.baseline: v1.1 rules (B+0) with no age term

candidate.remedy tested: rating - points_per_year x max(0, age - from_age), grid from_age 28 to 36, 5 to 80 points per year, plus quadratic forms

results.shape: the gain grows down to from_age 28 and flattens between 20 and 40 points per year; quadratic forms are no better
results.by division (favourite 35+): welterweight 42% (121), heavyweight 45% (115), middleweight 48% (90), lightweight 41% (83), light heavyweight 50% (80), bantamweight 39% (61), featherweight 49% (53)
results.age difference gradient (favourite minus: favourite 5+ years younger: wins 70.0% (729); 2-5 younger 64.9% (690); within 2 years 57.3% (1,048); 2-5 older 53.6% (623); 5+ older 40.7% (627)
results.large score gaps only (above the median: favourite 35+ wins 49.9% (355) against 65% for younger favourites: the board's confidence in an older fighter is worth nothing

face_validity.today, 33 / 20 (mildest): Usman 8 (v1.1: 5), Buckley 13, Edwards 7, Muhammad 14, Adesanya 25 (14), Whittaker 10, Blachowicz 34 (13), Vera 15, Ortega 26 (15), Cejudo 52, Oliveira 1, Holloway 2, Jim Miller 63 (19), Perez 27, Chiasson 7
face_validity.today, 32 / 30: Usman 16, Buckley 12, Adesanya 28, Blachowicz 42, Vera 21, Ortega 35
face_validity.welterweight top 10 at 33 / 20: Makhachev C, Prates, Morales, Brady, Garry, Della Maddalena, Bonfim, Edwards, Usman, Malott, Donchenko
face_validity.conflict: the curator wants long resumes (Adesanya, Blachowicz, Ortega) to stay in the top 15; every age setting that helps accuracy moves them down

reason: Rejected for the board by the curator on principle (Oct 20, 2026): REAL ranks who has earned the spot as of now, not who wins next. A resume rank lags ability by construction, since a contender earns the higher spot by beating the man who holds it, and an older top-10 fighter loses more often because he is matched against the best, which is the point of the board. Predictive concordance therefore punishes the lag and is a descriptive check, not the objective (PREREGISTRATION.md section 8). The finding stays as a measured property for the paper, and age belongs in the prediction model (the shadow model carries age terms). What would change the verdict: a decision to publish a separate contender board; the age_discount option in build() and the harness remains available for that.

title: Glicko-1 rating deviation for the resume rating: parameter derivation and calibration
question: Can a per-fighter rating deviation (RD) be attached to the resume rating that separates a one-bout newcomer from a twenty-bout veteran, and are its widths consistent with outcomes?

method.instrument: src/mmalab/uncertainty.py (Glicko-1 formulas on the engine's pre-fight ratings; display only, never ordering)
method.window: all 8,950 bouts to Oct 17, 2026 (2,776 fighters); calibration on 5,817 decided bouts since 2015
method.metric: RD distribution by career bouts; favourite win rate by standardised rating gap in 8 equal-count bins against the Glicko expectation; log loss of the plain gap vs the Glicko-shrunk gap
method.interval: bin standard error about 0.018; mean bias standard error about 0.006

shipped.rule: information balance: RD^2 added between bouts at the median cadence equals what one typical bout removes from an established fighter

rejected.rule: Glicko's t = 5 years from the median 10th-bout RD, iterated to a fixed point

results.same at c = 130.2: 290; 247; 215; 199 (a 20-bout veteran no better measured than a 7-bout fighter: rejected)
results.today's board: rd >= 200 flags exactly the 212 fighters with 1-3 bouts plus 7 four-bout fighters; median RD 235 for top-30 slots held by fighters with 3 or fewer bouts vs 120 for 10+
results.band width: a 1-RD band spans 5 or more positions for 99% of the board because the within-division rating SD (about 95) is about one veteran RD; median span 56 positions (42 in the top 30)
results.calibration: favourites win more often than the Glicko expectation in 7 of 8 bins (bias +0.019 at c = 37.3, +0.026 at c = 130; the plain Elo gap is unbiased at +0.003 and has the lower log loss, 0.6781 vs 0.6795 to 0.6802); gap slope 0.95 of nominal (0.87 when both fighters have 3+ bouts)
results.no-mutation check: run_resume outputs byte-identical with and without the module

face_validity.Lightweight today: Oliveira 1860 RD 105 band ranks 1-4; Topuria 1792 RD 132 band 1-14; Pimblett 1720 RD 132 band 3-31; a one-bout newcomer at 1545 RD 291 spans the whole division

reason: RD is attached to every board row as a measurement-information statement (bouts fought, opponents' certainty, time idle) and drives nothing in the order. It is not a predictive shrinkage: applying g() to an Elo-type gap double-shrinks, and debutants are over-rated at 1500 (a bias, not a variance). Showing rank bands would mislead (almost every band spans 5+ places); the experience contrast is the usable signal and backs the provisional label.
notes: Worth remembering: Glicko's t = 5 rule is incompatible with a usable experience gradient in UFC data (about 2 bouts a year, d of about 412 points per bout). A grace-period inflation (idle time beyond 0.5 years at c of about 146) would give both a gradient at normal cadence and a reset after a long layoff; not implemented.

title: Placement layer as one constrained order (solver) versus the sequential head-to-head and title-cycle loops
question: Do the two placement rules, applied one after the other, produce an order that satisfies their own constraints, and does solving them together change the published boards?

method.instrument: src/mmalab/placement.py (priority topological sort over precedence and cap constraints collected against the score order) against resume_board.head_to_head then title_cycle, on captured build inputs
method.metric: positions differing; constraints violated by each method; waived lifts; lifts the sequential rule applied that do not qualify against the score order
method.script: scripts/verify_placement.py (regenerates every table from live builds)

candidate.semantics kept: most recent meeting within 3 years lifts the winner directly above the loser when he sits within 3 places (6 if within a year); old close wins void the pair; a negative last five forfeits; title-cycle losers capped at 4 with their recent victims held below them
candidate.cycles: broken by dropping the oldest meeting (none in real data)

results.positions differing: 65 of 4,862 (33 of 1,155 top-15) across 13 of 77 divisions
results.sequential violates its own constraints: 10 cases: 6 chain inversions, 2 missed lifts, 2 caps overriding an older head-to-head
results.today's lightweight: sequential: Oliveira 1, Holloway 2, Topuria 3 although Topuria knocked Oliveira out on 2025-06-28; solver: Topuria 1, Oliveira 2, Holloway 3
results.non-qualifying lifts by the sequential r: 6 (a lift that only qualified after an earlier lift moved the loser)
results.settled results inverted across 4,404 pa: sequential 11, solver 6 (all six are winners held by a cap or victim rule)
results.determinism: shuffle tests over 40 random constraint sets and every real division

face_validity.today, v1.1 sequential vs solver: 17 positions differ, 6 in a top 15: Lightweight Topuria 3 to 1, Oliveira 1 to 2, Holloway 2 to 3; Women's Bantamweight Dumont 5 to 3, Vieira 3 to 4, Cavalcanti 4 to 5
face_validity.reach of transitive chains: Marco Tulio +8 at middleweight today, Castaneda +7 in Sept 2024, inherent in treating the constraints as hard

reason: Adopted for board v1.1 (config resume.placement: solver), amended into PREREGISTRATION.md appendix C before the first v1.1 snapshot; the sequential loops stay as v1.0's frozen rule. The solver honours the same rules without order dependence; every difference from the sequential result is a case where the sequential result broke one of its own constraints or applied a lift that did not qualify.

title: v1.1 as shipped (loss tiers, form, protection 0.30, placement solver) on 43 full boards, corrected data
question: With the dated roster files, the official-rank aliases and the same-name split in place, and the placement solver included, is v1.1 at least as accurate as v1.0 on full event-eve boards?

method.instrument: resume_board.build at every third event date with every placement rule applied (v1.0: sequential loops; v1.1: solver), published order
method.bouts: 979 decided bouts between two fighters on the same divisional board (973 to 979 depending on eligibility under each version; paired by bout)
method.metric: concordance of the published order; log loss with the frozen slope 1.36
method.baseline: v1.0 on the same bouts and the same corrected data

candidate: config/board_v1_1.yaml as committed on Oct 20, 2026 (overrides: protected_loss_mult 0.30; loss_tiers [[5,0.25],[10,0.5],[15,0.75],[999,1.0]], dominant_extra 0; form_penalty 0.10/0.30/0.40; form_bad_loss rank_above 10, 0.10 per loss, cap 0.30; placement solver)

results.paired v1.1 minus v1.0: concordance -0.0010 (CI -0.0189 to +0.0164); log loss -0.0045 (CI -0.0093 to +0.0001); top-15 concordance +0.0000 (CI -0.034 to +0.035) on 246 bouts

reason: Equal measured accuracy with a small log-loss edge; v1.1 ships as the shadow resume board under appendix C (non-inferiority). Supersedes the numbers in EXP-2026-10-20-01 for the changelog.
